topics: Law of Sines, Cosines & SSA ambiguity

body.en: Standardized Level 1 tests demand fluency well beyond basic right-triangle trigonometry (SOHCAHTOA). Topics include radian measure conversions, the unit circle with all special angles, Pythagorean and double-angle identities, angle addition formulas, inverse trig principal branches, and oblique triangle laws including the ambiguous SSA case.

label.en: Definition 4.1 — Unit Circle, Circular Functions, and Arc Measures

body.en:
Essential definitions of circular trigonometry:
  • Radian Measure & Arc Length: For a circle of radius \(r\) and central angle \(\theta\) in radians:
    \[ s = r\theta, \qquad A = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta \]Conversion: \(\theta_{\text{rad}} = \theta_{\text{deg}} \times \frac{\pi}{180^\circ}\), \(\theta_{\text{deg}} = \theta_{\text{rad}} \times \frac{180^\circ}{\pi}\).
  • Unit Circle Coordinates: On the unit circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\), an angle \(\theta\) in standard position defines coordinates:
    \[ x = \cos\theta, \qquad y = \sin\theta, \qquad \tan\theta = \frac{y}{x} = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} \; (x \neq 0) \]Reciprocal functions: \(\sec\theta = \frac{1}{\cos\theta}\), \(\csc\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta}\), \(\cot\theta = \frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\).
  • Signs by Quadrant (CAST / ASTC Rule):
    Quadrant I (\(0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\)): All positive (\(\sin, \cos, \tan > 0\)).
    Quadrant II (\(\frac{\pi}{2} < \theta < \pi\)): Sine positive; cosine and tangent negative.
    Quadrant III (\(\pi < \theta < \frac{3\pi}{2}\)): Tangent positive; sine and cosine negative.
    Quadrant IV (\(\frac{3\pi}{2} < \theta < 2\pi\)): Cosine positive; sine and tangent negative.

caption.en: Unit circle coordinates for \( \theta = 120^\circ = \frac{2\pi}{3}\text{ rad} \). The terminal point has coordinates \( (\cos 120^\circ, \sin 120^\circ) = \left(-\frac{1}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \) with reference angle \( 60^\circ \) in Quadrant II.

label.en: Theorem 4.1 — Trigonometric Identities and Inverse Functions

body.en:
Key identities and principal ranges for standardized exams:
  • Pythagorean Identities:
    \[ \sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1, \qquad 1 + \tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta, \qquad 1 + \cot^2\theta = \csc^2\theta \]
  • Double-Angle Formulas:
    \[ \sin(2\theta) = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta \]\[ \cos(2\theta) = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta - 1 = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta \]\[ \tan(2\theta) = \frac{2\tan\theta}{1 - \tan^2\theta} \]
  • Angle Addition and Subtraction:
    \[ \sin(\alpha \pm \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta \pm \cos\alpha\sin\beta \]\[ \cos(\alpha \pm \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta \mp \sin\alpha\sin\beta \]\[ \tan(\alpha \pm \beta) = \frac{\tan\alpha \pm \tan\beta}{1 \mp \tan\alpha\tan\beta} \]
  • Inverse Trigonometric Principal Branches:
    \(\arcsin(x)\): Domain \([-1, 1]\), Range \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\).
    \(\arccos(x)\): Domain \([-1, 1]\), Range \([0, \pi]\).
    \(\arctan(x)\): Domain \((-\infty, \infty)\), Range \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\).

label.en: ● Law of Sines, Cosines & Triangle Solving

body.en:
For any triangle with side lengths \(a, b, c\) opposite angles \(A, B, C\):
  • Law of Sines:
    \[ \frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B} = \frac{c}{\sin C} = 2R \quad (R = \text{circumradius}) \]Used for AAS, ASA, and SSA cases.
  • The Ambiguous Case (SSA): When given \(a, b\) and acute angle \(A\):
    If \(a < b\sin A\): \(0\) triangles exist (side \(a\) cannot reach the opposite side).
    If \(a = b\sin A\): \(1\) right triangle exists.
    If \(b\sin A < a < b\): \(2\) distinct triangles exist (one with acute \(B\), one with obtuse \(B' = 180^\circ - B\)).
    If \(a \ge b\): \(1\) triangle exists.
  • Law of Cosines:
    \[ c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C \iff \cos C = \frac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab} \]Used for SAS and SSS cases.
  • Triangle Area: \(K = \frac{1}{2}ab\sin C = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}\) where semiperimeter \(s = \frac{a+b+c}{2}\).

label.en: ▲ ACT Math 2 Traps & Pitfalls — Trigonometry & Angle Measures

body.en:
• Radian vs. Degree Calculator Mode: ACT questions mix degrees (e.g. \(120°\)) and radians (e.g. \(2\pi/3\)). Check your calculator mode before every trig calculation! If you get unexpected decimals for standard values, check the mode first.
  • Inverse Trig Output Ranges: \(\arcsin(x)\) can ONLY return angles in \([-\pi/2, \pi/2]\) (Quadrants I and IV with negative angles). If \(\sin\theta = -1/2\), \(\arcsin(-1/2) = -\pi/6\), NOT \(11\pi/6\) or \(7\pi/6\). Likewise \(\arccos(x) \in [0, \pi]\).
  • The Ambiguous Case (SSA): When using the Law of Sines with two sides and an acute non-included angle (SSA), always verify whether the supplementary angle \(180^\circ - B\) satisfies \(A + (180^\circ - B) < 180^\circ\). If so, two distinct valid triangles exist.
  • Double-Angle Cosine Substitutions: Always select the form of \(\cos(2\theta)\) that matches your equation's other terms: use \(1 - 2\sin^2\theta\) if the rest contains \(\sin\theta\), and \(2\cos^2\theta - 1\) if the rest contains \(\cos\theta\).

label.en: Worked Example 4.A — Exact Trigonometric Value via Angle Addition

body.en:
Evaluate the exact value of \(\cos(105^\circ)\) without using a decimal approximation.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Express \(105^\circ\) as a sum of special unit circle angles:
    \[ 105^\circ = 60^\circ + 45^\circ \]
  2. Apply the cosine addition formula \(\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta\):
    \[ \cos(60^\circ + 45^\circ) = \cos 60^\circ \cos 45^\circ - \sin 60^\circ \sin 45^\circ \]
  3. Substitute known exact values from the unit circle:
    \[ \cos 60^\circ = \frac{1}{2}, \quad \cos 45^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}, \quad \sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, \quad \sin 45^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \]
  4. Multiply and combine over a common denominator:
    \[ \cos(105^\circ) = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) - \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{6}}{4} \]
The exact value is \(\mathbf{\frac{\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{6}}{4}}\).

label.en: Worked Example 4.B — Law of Cosines and Unknown Side Computation

body.en:
In \(\triangle ABC\), side \(a = 7\), side \(b = 10\), and the included angle \(C = 60^\circ\). Calculate the exact value of side \(c\) and approximate it to two decimal places.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Identify the known values: two sides and the included angle (SAS configuration). Apply the Law of Cosines:
    \[ c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C \]
  2. Substitute \(a = 7\), \(b = 10\), and \(C = 60^\circ\):
    \[ c^2 = 7^2 + 10^2 - 2(7)(10)\cos(60^\circ) \]\[ c^2 = 49 + 100 - 140 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 149 - 70 = 79 \]
  3. Take the positive square root for a side length:
    \[ c = \sqrt{79} \approx 8.888 \approx \mathbf{8.89} \]
Side \(c = \mathbf{\sqrt{79} \approx 8.89}\).

label.en: Worked Example 4.C — Solving Trigonometric Equations via Double-Angle Identities

body.en:
Solve the equation \(\cos(2\theta) + 3\sin\theta - 2 = 0\) for all solutions \(\theta \in [0, 2\pi)\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Replace \(\cos(2\theta)\) with the identity in terms of \(\sin\theta\): \(\cos(2\theta) = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta\):
    \[ (1 - 2\sin^2\theta) + 3\sin\theta - 2 = 0 \]\[ -2\sin^2\theta + 3\sin\theta - 1 = 0 \]Multiply by \(-1\):
    \[ 2\sin^2\theta - 3\sin\theta + 1 = 0 \]
  2. Factor the quadratic in \(\sin\theta\):
    \[ (2\sin\theta - 1)(\sin\theta - 1) = 0 \]
  3. Solve each linear factor:
    Factor 1: \(2\sin\theta - 1 = 0 \implies \sin\theta = \frac{1}{2}\). On \([0, 2\pi)\), sine is positive in Quadrants I and II with reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{6}\):
    \[ \theta = \frac{\pi}{6}, \qquad \theta = \pi - \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{5\pi}{6} \]
    Factor 2: \(\sin\theta - 1 = 0 \implies \sin\theta = 1\). On \([0, 2\pi)\):
    \[ \theta = \frac{\pi}{2} \]
The complete solution set on \([0, 2\pi)\) is \(\mathbf{\left\{ \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{5\pi}{6} \right\}}\).

question.en: Prove the trigonometric identity \(\dfrac{1-\cos 2\theta}{\sin 2\theta} = \tan\theta\) for all values of \(\theta\) where both sides are defined.

solution.en:
Step 1: Substitute the double-angle identities \(\cos 2\theta = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta\) and \(\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta\):
\[ \frac{1 - (1 - 2\sin^2\theta)}{2\sin\theta\cos\theta} \]

Step 2: Simplify the numerator:
\[ 1 - 1 + 2\sin^2\theta = 2\sin^2\theta \]

Step 3: Form the ratio and cancel common factor \(2\sin\theta\) (for \(\sin\theta \neq 0\)):
\[ \frac{2\sin^2\theta}{2\sin\theta\cos\theta} = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \mathbf{\tan\theta} \quad \blacksquare \]

question.en: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(a = 6\), \(b = 10\), and angle \(A = 30^\circ\). Determine how many possible triangles exist, and find the possible value(s) of angle \(B\) in degrees.

solution.en:
Step 1 (Check SSA Ambiguity): Compute the altitude from vertex \(C\):
\[ h = b\sin A = 10\sin(30^\circ) = 10\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 5 \]
Compare the opposite side \(a = 6\) with \(h\) and \(b\):
\[ h < a < b \implies 5 < 6 < 10 \]
Since \(h < a < b\), exactly two distinct triangles exist.

Step 2 (Find \(B_1\) and \(B_2\)): Use the Law of Sines:
\[ \frac{\sin B}{b} = \frac{\sin A}{a} \implies \sin B = \frac{10\sin(30^\circ)}{6} = \frac{5}{6} \approx 0.8333 \]\[ B_1 = \arcsin\left(\frac{5}{6}\right) \approx \mathbf{56.4^\circ} \]
The obtuse supplementary angle is:
\[ B_2 = 180^\circ - 56.4^\circ = \mathbf{123.6^\circ} \]
Check validity: \(A + B_2 = 30^\circ + 123.6^\circ = 153.6^\circ < 180^\circ\), which is valid.

Let \(\alpha = \arcsin\left(-\frac{3}{5}\right)\) and \(\beta = \arctan(2)\). By definition:
\(\alpha \in [-\pi/2, 0]\) (Quadrant IV), \(\sin\alpha = -\frac{3}{5} \implies \cos\alpha = \sqrt{1 - (-3/5)^2} = \frac{4}{5}\).
\(\beta \in (0, \pi/2)\) (Quadrant I), \(\tan\beta = \frac{2}{1} \implies \text{hypotenuse} = \sqrt{1^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{5}\), so \(\sin\beta = \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\), \(\cos\beta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\).

Apply the cosine addition formula \(\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta\):
\[ \cos(\alpha + \beta) = \left(\frac{4}{5}\right)\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right) - \left(-\frac{3}{5}\right)\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right) = \frac{4 + 6}{5\sqrt{5}} = \frac{10}{5\sqrt{5}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} = \mathbf{\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}} \]

question.en: Find all solutions to \(2\cos^2\theta - \cos\theta - 1 = 0\) on the interval \([0, 2\pi)\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Factor the quadratic equation in \(\cos\theta\):
\[ (2\cos\theta + 1)(\cos\theta - 1) = 0 \]

Step 2: Set each factor to zero:
Case 1: \(2\cos\theta + 1 = 0 \implies \cos\theta = -\frac{1}{2}\).
Cosine is negative in Quadrants II and III with reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\):
\[ \theta = \pi - \frac{\pi}{3} = \mathbf{\frac{2\pi}{3}}, \qquad \theta = \pi + \frac{\pi}{3} = \mathbf{\frac{4\pi}{3}} \]
Case 2: \(\cos\theta - 1 = 0 \implies \cos\theta = 1\).
On \([0, 2\pi)\), \(\cos\theta = 1\) at \(\theta = \mathbf{0}\).

Final Solution Set: \(\mathbf{\left\{ 0, \frac{2\pi}{3}, \frac{4\pi}{3} \right\}}\).
